Subject: 4 stars - Lanternfolk would not exist without Murmur, but use 3.1.4 and not 3.2

I have used Murmur since 2022 (bought it at v1.3), and I'm writing this because the reviews from the last two weeks only tell half of it.

First the part new buyers need to know, because the bad reviews are right about this.

3.2.0 has a real save bug. If you load a save that was made in 3.1.x, every Murmur variable is back to its default value. In our game that means the ferryman forgets you already paid him. I only tested with saves from 3.1.x and then rolled back, so I can't tell you how saves made in 3.2 itself behave. The version on the listing right now is 3.2.0, and Ines has said it is the last one she will make. So there is no fix coming from her and no support.

The fix that works for us and for others in the forum:

1. Get the 3.1.4 release.
2. In your project, replace the Murmur folder in addons with the 3.1.4 one.
3. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 somewhere safe and don't update to 3.2.

After that our old saves loaded fine again. There is more in my forum thread here ("3.2.0: variables reset to default after loading a save"). Thanks tobbe_codes for confirming it.

If you are starting a new project and you need someone to answer when things break, this is honestly not the tool for you right now. I won't pretend it is. That's why 4 stars and not 5.

Now the other half.

The first prototype of Lanternfolk was the ferryman scene. I made it in one weekend in 2022 with Murmur, and that was when I quit my job at a mobile studio. Today the game has 412 dialogue nodes in 9 languages, all through Murmur's CSV export, and we are shipping it on 3.1.4. Nothing else I have bought for this game did so much of the work.

I paid 19 dollars for that. Once, for unlimited commercial projects, and then the updates kept coming for four years.

One review here says she took our money and ran. I get being angry about broken saves, I really do. But she didn't run. She put a note on the listing, said sorry for the bug, and put the whole source on the public repo under MIT so the tool can live on without her. People who run don't do that.

And that's the hopeful part. It's MIT now, so anyone can fork it and fix the save bug. Maybe that will even be me, once Lanternfolk is out. No promises.

Ines, thank you for four years. My game is built on your work.
